<objective>
Give a named human's decision a recorded form: a `withdrawn, by human:<name>: <reason>` History entry may close an `open` build request. Today the grammar refuses it as `bad-transition`, so the only legal close of an open request is a BA/PM-alone line, and a human who decides at a floor stop to drop the request has no record (gap G-45-9, debug session floor-prohibition-weak, evidence entry 17:32).

This is the human's routing choice at UAT on 2026-11-26 (decision 1, GRAMMAR CHANGE). It refines D-06: BA/PM may still withdraw an open request alone, and the grammar does not decide which open requests need a human. That is a prose rule plan 45-13 writes into Workflow 20, because a request file carries no field that marks it a deviation or a floor conflict (D-05 closed key set).

Reversibility: costly, already settled by the human at UAT, so no new checkpoint. A file written with the new line is refused by a runnable built before this plan; RUNNABLE_SET_STAMP moves, so version skew is reported, never silently passed. v3.1 is unreleased, so no installed host holds the older grammar.

Purpose: the human's word at a floor stop or a deviation can be written down in the actor slot, where the grammar and every reader see it.
Output: the grammar change with RED/GREEN tests, regenerated embeds and builds, and the contract's forms.
</objective>

From scripts/build-request-model.ts (the History state machine, about lines 585-660):
- Each History item is parsed by buildRequestHistoryEntry into { date, event, actor, pin?, line }. `human` is true when `entry.actor !== BUILD_REQUEST_AGENT_ACTOR` (the agent actor is the string `BA/PM`; a human actor is a HUMAN_STAMP_RE stamp).
- The final else-arm handles `withdrawn`. Today it computes the wanted actor from `state` (open wants BA/PM, carried wants a human) and refuses anything else with `bad-transition`. Its reason names the line and the rule and quotes no file text.
- Earlier arms already refuse: an entry after `answered` or `withdrawn`; a second `open`; an `edited` entry by a human stamp; `carried` or `answered` without a human stamp; `answered` from `open`.

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| agent → build-request state | BA/PM writes every History line; a `human:<name>` stamp records a human's word in prose, not by authentication |
| older installed runnable → newer request file | a host running a runnable built before this plan reads a file that holds the new line |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-45-36 | Spoofing | `withdrawn, by human:<name>` on an open request | medium | mitigate | the contract keeps its sentence that `human:<name>` is a prose-tier record and not authentication; plan 45-13's Workflow 20 stop bullet refuses an agent's withdrawal of a deviation or floor-conflict request without a named human's word; the git host and review remain the check on who changed the file |
| T-45-37 | Elevation of privilege | the History state machine | high | mitigate | Task 1 changes only the withdrawn arm; tests keep `carried` and `answered` human-only and a BA/PM withdrawal of a carried request refused (D-06, Pitfall 6) |
| T-45-38 | Denial of service | an older installed `state-check.js` or `upstream.js` | low | accept | it refuses the new line as `bad-transition` with exit 2, which is surfaced and never read as a pass; RUNNABLE_SET_STAMP moves, so skew is reported; v3.1 is unreleased |
| T-45-39 | Information disclosure | refusal reasons | low | mitigate | the new reason names the line and the rule only, built like its neighbours; the value-silence table keeps a `bad-transition` row with a planted marker |
| T-45-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | low | accept | this plan installs no package |
</threat_model>
